transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is my sleep has just gotten really unreliable. I don’t want to make it sound overly dramatic, but even when I’m exhausted and go to bed, I end up lying there replaying work forecasts and team issues in my head. Then I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 and it’s like my brain just won’t power down again. I’m not sure if that’s the right kind of thing to come in for, but it’s been getting hard to manage.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're lying awake at night replaying work forecasts and team issues?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m panicking or anything, but I do feel worried. Most days my mind kind of jumps from one thing to another — like whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, or if someone on my team is about to quit, then suddenly I’m thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. It’s like every small delay starts to feel like it could turn into something major. I don’t know if that makes sense, but that’s usually what’s happening when I’m awake.
Is this worry about work and other things something that happens throughout the day, or is it mainly at night when you're trying to sleep?

It’s… not only at night, no. I wish it were just when I’m trying to sleep, because that would feel a little more contained. But during the day, most days, my mind kind of hops from one worry to the next — like whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, then whether someone on my team might be about to quit, then the mortgage, or a client renewal.

I know some of that is normal work stress, and I don’t want to overstate it, but even small delays can start feeling like they’re going to turn into something much bigger. Does that make sense?
Is the sleep problem what's been bothering you the most, or is it the worry and anxiety that's really the main issue for you?

I think… if I’m being honest, it’s probably the worry more than the sleep itself. The sleep is what made me feel like I should come in, because it’s easier to point to, I guess.

But during most days my mind jumps around — like, will we hit the launch numbers, is someone on my team going to quit, what about the mortgage, or that client renewal — and then some small delay starts feeling like it could turn into something much bigger. I know that might just sound like normal responsibility, but it feels like it’s taking up a lot of space in my head.
Is this worry and anxiety mainly focused on work, or does it also affect other areas of your life?

It’s mostly work, I think… or that’s where it starts, anyway. Like the launch numbers or whether someone on my team is unhappy, that kind of thing.

But it doesn’t really stay neatly in that box. It’ll jump to the mortgage, or a client renewal, and then I’m treating some small delay like it’s a sign something bigger is going wrong. I know that probably sounds a little dramatic, but it feels hard to shut off once it starts.
Do you usually feel anxious or worried even when you're not thinking about work or specific problems like the mortgage?

Yeah… I think so. Maybe not “worried” in a clear, specific way all the time, but I feel kind of wound up even when nothing is actually happening.

Like I can be at home eating dinner, and my body still feels like I’m sitting in a pipeline review or waiting for bad news. My shoulders stay tight a lot, even when I’m trying to relax. I don’t know if that counts as anxiety exactly, but it doesn’t feel like I fully switch off.
You mentioned feeling wound up even when trying to relax, does that feeling of being wound up go away at any point during the day?

Not really… I mean, I wish I could say it does. It might ease up a little if I’m distracted, but even then I still feel kind of wound up underneath.

Like I’ll be at home eating dinner and it’s not like anything is actively happening, but my body still feels like I’m in a pipeline review or waiting for something to go wrong. My shoulders stay tight a lot, even when I’m trying to relax. I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right, but it feels pretty constant.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're in situations that don't involve work or the things you mentioned like mortgages or client renewals?

Yeah… I think it does, though I keep wanting to say it’s just “practical stuff,” you know?

It’s like my mind will start with work — whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, or whether someone on my team is unhappy or about to leave — but then it doesn’t stop there. It jumps to the mortgage, or whether a client renewal is going to fall through, and then even a small delay starts to feel like it could turn into something much bigger.

So… yes, I guess it shows up outside of work too. I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is, but it does kind of spread.
Does your anxiety or worry tend to follow any kind of pattern or cycle throughout the day?

I don’t know if it’s a clean pattern exactly… it’s more like loops, if that makes sense.

I’ll tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve already made the plan, you’ve done what you can, just let it go,” and I can mean that in the moment. But then five minutes later I’m back in it again, turning over some other angle. I’ll mentally check one concern off, and then three more pop up.

So I guess the cycle is… I try to reassure myself, it helps briefly, and then my mind finds the next thing. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're doing things you normally enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends and family?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t enjoy anything, because I can, or at least I try to.

But even if I’m doing something nice or spending time with people, my mind can still kind of drift back. Like, are we going to hit the launch numbers, is someone on my team unhappy or about to quit, what if the mortgage becomes an issue, what if that client renewal doesn’t come through… and then some small delay starts feeling bigger than it probably is.

So yes, I guess it can be there even during things I’m supposed to be enjoying. Is that what you mean?
Is there ever a time or situation when you feel completely free from worry or anxiety?

Completely free? Um… I’d like to say yes, and I’m sure there are moments where I’m distracted enough that it quiets down.

But most days, no, not completely. My mind just sort of jumps around — first it’s whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, then whether someone on my team is unhappy or about to leave, then the mortgage, or a client renewal… and even a small delay can start to feel like it might turn into something major.

I know that probably sounds like a lot. I don’t mean that I’m panicking every second, just… it’s hard to find a time where there’s nothing running in the background.
Is your worry and anxiety present even when you're not thinking about sleep or trying to fall asleep?

Yes… it’s not just at bedtime or when I’m trying to sleep.

I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days my mind sort of hops from one thing to the next — like whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, or if someone on my team is unhappy and might quit, then the mortgage, or whether a client renewal is going to come through. And then even a small delay can start feeling like it could become something much bigger.

So… yes, it’s there during the day too, not only around sleep. Is that answering what you’re asking?
Is there anything in particular that you think triggers your worry and anxiety, or does it seem to come up on its own without any specific cause?

I think there are definitely things that set it off, like anything around work numbers or the team… but honestly it also kind of comes up on its own sometimes.

Most days my mind just jumps from, you know, are we going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team is upset or thinking of leaving, then suddenly I’m thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. And then if there’s even a small delay, I start imagining it turning into something much bigger.

I know some of that is probably normal stress, so I don’t want to overstate it, but… it feels like my brain is always finding the next thing to worry about. Does that make sense?
Is your worry and anxiety focused on a specific set of concerns, like work and finances, or does it feel more general, like you're worried about everything in general?

It’s probably more centered on work and finances, I guess… at least those are the things I can name most easily.

Like, my mind goes from whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team is unhappy or might quit, then it’s the mortgage, or a client renewal. And sometimes even a small delay starts feeling like it could turn into something really major.

I don’t think I’m worried about literally everything, but it does feel like my brain can turn a lot of things into a problem pretty quickly. Does that make sense?
Is your worry and anxiety mainly about specific things like work, finances, and relationships, or does it feel like you're worried about almost everything in general?

I think it’s mostly specific things, like work and money stuff… and maybe people on my team, if that counts as relationships.

But it doesn’t stay neatly in one box, if that makes sense. Most days my mind jumps from whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team is about to quit, then suddenly I’m thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. And then even a small delay can start feeling like it’s going to turn into something major.

I know everyone worries about those things, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is… but it does feel like my brain keeps finding the next thing. Is that kind of what you mean?
Do you think your worry and anxiety could be described as being about almost everything in general, or is it mostly focused on specific areas like work and finances?

I’d say it’s mostly focused on specific areas, like work and finances… though it can feel pretty broad once it starts.

Most days, my mind jumps from whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team is about to quit, then to the mortgage or a client renewal. And then if there’s some small delay, I can start picturing it turning into something major.

I know those are normal things to care about, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it does feel like my brain keeps moving to the next possible problem.
Is your worry about many different things in life or mostly about work and a few specific issues like finances?

Mostly work and a few specific things, I think… work is definitely the big one, and then finances kind of gets pulled in.

Most days my mind goes from, like, are we going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team might be unhappy or about to quit, and then I’m thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. And if there’s even a small delay, I can start feeling like it’s going to turn into something much bigger.

I don’t know if that counts as “many different things” or just a few categories, but that’s sort of how it feels.
Is your worry and anxiety usually about a specific issue or problem, or is it a more general feeling of unease that isn't focused on one particular thing?

It’s probably more specific than just a general uneasy feeling, I think. Work is usually where it starts.

Like, most days my mind goes from whether we’re going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team might quit, and then I’m suddenly thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. And I know those are real things to think about, but sometimes even a small delay feels like it could turn into something major.

So… I guess it’s focused on certain problems, but it can spread pretty quickly. Does that make sense?
Are you able to completely relax and feel no anxiety when you're engaged in an activity that you find enjoyable and calming?

I can relax a little, especially if I’m doing something calming, but… completely relax? Probably not, if I’m being honest.

Even at home, like if I’m just eating dinner or trying to watch something, I still feel kind of wound up, almost like I’m sitting in a pipeline review. My shoulders stay tight, and I have to remind myself to unclench, which sounds silly. It’s not like I’m panicking the whole time, but I don’t really get to that “no anxiety at all” place very often. Does that answer it okay?
Has there been a specific stressful event or change in your life that you think might have triggered these feelings of anxiety and worry?

I think it probably started with the sales division reorganization… or at least that’s when I noticed it building.

It was about thirteen months ago now, and I don’t want to make it sound like one huge dramatic event, because people go through work changes all the time, but after that shift I just never really seemed to settle back down. The worry kind of kept growing from there.

Does that make sense as a trigger?

target_item.manifestation: Most days my mind jumps from whether we'll hit the launch numbers to whether someone on my team is about to quit, then to the mortgage or a client renewal, and it feels like every small delay could turn into something major.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the breadth and focus of the patient's worry across different life areas, which directly matches excessive anxiety and worry about a number of events or activities.

patient.answer:
Mostly work and a few specific things, I think… work is definitely the big one, and then finances kind of gets pulled in.

Most days my mind goes from, like, are we going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team might be unhappy or about to quit, and then I’m thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. And if there’s even a small delay, I can start feeling like it’s going to turn into something much bigger.

I don’t know if that counts as “many different things” or just a few categories, but that’s sort of how it feels.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's anxiety is generalized or specific to certain areas
doctor.question: Is your worry and anxiety usually about a specific issue or problem, or is it a more general feeling of unease that isn't focused on one particular thing?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: Most days my mind jumps from whether we'll hit the launch numbers to whether someone on my team is about to quit, then to the mortgage or a client renewal, and it feels like every small delay could turn into something major.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the anxiety is focused on specific problems or spread across multiple/general areas, which directly relates to excessive worry about a number of events or activities.

patient.answer:
It’s probably more specific than just a general uneasy feeling, I think. Work is usually where it starts.

Like, most days my mind goes from whether we’re going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team might quit, and then I’m suddenly thinking about the mortgage or a client renewal. And I know those are real things to think about, but sometimes even a small delay feels like it could turn into something major.

So… I guess it’s focused on certain problems, but it can spread pretty quickly. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: determine if anxiety is present during relaxation
doctor.question: Are you able to completely relax and feel no anxiety when you're engaged in an activity that you find enjoyable and calming?

target_item.name: Restlessness_Tension
target_item.manifestation: I feel wound up almost all the time, like I'm sitting in a pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner, and my shoulders stay tight no matter how much I try to relax.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether I can relax and feel free of anxiety during calming activities, which most directly relates to feeling keyed up, tense, or unable to relax.

patient.answer:
I can relax a little, especially if I’m doing something calming, but… completely relax? Probably not, if I’m being honest.

Even at home, like if I’m just eating dinner or trying to watch something, I still feel kind of wound up, almost like I’m sitting in a pipeline review. My shoulders stay tight, and I have to remind myself to unclench, which sounds silly. It’s not like I’m panicking the whole time, but I don’t really get to that “no anxiety at all” place very often. Does that answer it okay?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is better explained by a generalized anxiety disorder or an adjustment disorder with anxiety
doctor.question: Has there been a specific stressful event or change in your life that you think might have triggered these feelings of anxiety and worry?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been building since the sales division reorganization about thirteen months ago.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether a specific life change triggered the anxiety, which is covered by the duration item noting it has been building since the sales division reorganization about thirteen months ago.

patient.answer:
I think it probably started with the sales division reorganization… or at least that’s when I noticed it building.

It was about thirteen months ago now, and I don’t want to make it sound like one huge dramatic event, because people go through work changes all the time, but after that shift I just never really seemed to settle back down. The worry kind of kept growing from there.

Does that make sense as a trigger?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of excessive worry about everyday things, such as work and finances, for more than six months, and the impact of these symptoms on their daily life, align with the diagnostic criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).
